solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person helping pianist with compelling work?

definitions.meaning: someone who sits beside a performer flipping the sheets of music at the right moment
a gripping book you cannot put down, read eagerly to the end

explanation.surface: Someone assisting a pianist on a piece of absorbing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the assistant who flips sheet music, and the informal term for an unputdownable book.

clue.text: Game in south coast town, on the radio

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the town's name is taken as spoken

parts.note: Poole is a harbour town in Dorset on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A sport played in a seaside town, as heard on a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue game played on a table with pockets, like billiards or snooker.

clue.text: Drink that may get soldier and general drunk

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

indicators.note: a drunk word is reeling about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A beverage that could leave a private and a general intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the soldiers after their drink, but it is what jumbles the word general.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Brusque, in sister's estimation

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words sister's estimation, running across the join

explanation.surface: Someone is curt, according to their sibling's judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech that is short, abrupt and rather unfriendly.

clue.text: Runs one downhiller maybe finds more dangerous

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one
a downhill racer is one example of a skier

explanation.surface: A downhill racer discovers that some slopes are more perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier is the comparative of risky, meaning more hazardous or dangerous.

clue.text: Cream cakes — girl's got her sixth in her mouth!

indicators.text: got her sixth in her mouth
indicators.note: the sixth letter of the name is shifted to the front, the mouth or opening of the word

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name, and with the 's it gives the letters CLAIRES

explanation.surface: A young woman has crammed her sixth pastry into her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth letter of CLAIRES is E; moving it to the head ('in her mouth') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long choux pastries filled with cream and topped with chocolate icing.

clue.text: Superior role over in the Beehive state

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior

indicators.note: over signals that the word for role is turned back to front

parts.note: to wear a particular hat is to take on a role

explanation.surface: An upper-class part played in a western American state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beehive State is the official nickname of Utah, the beehive being its emblem of industry.

clue.text: I chewed up a bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the preceding words are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, so chewed

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having gnawed a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I BIT into TIBI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Present journal includes most original of titbits passed on

parts.note: to be present is to be here

indicators.note: the journal word holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: the most original letter is the very first one

explanation.surface: A current magazine carries the very best of its snippets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits are passed on from parent to child, inherited down the generations.

clue.text: One who has depressant drug needs day off

indicators.note: off says the letter for day is removed from the drug word

parts.note: a downer is slang for a sedative or depressant drug

explanation.surface: Someone taking a sedative needs a day off work.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a possessor, one who has something as their property.

clue.text: Drink in here? Shop stocks nothing but

indicators.note: the shop stocks, or holds, the letter for nothing

parts.note: a salon is a hairdresser's or beauty shop
O is zero, nothing
bar means except or but, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A shop sells nothing but stuff to drink inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The saloon bar was the more comfortable lounge of a British pub, where you might take a drink.

clue.text: Crime of receiver

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: The offence committed by someone handling stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a crime.

clue.text: Retired professors from Cambridge ultimately deserve one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Cambridge

parts.note: to merit something is to deserve it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Retired academics at Cambridge eventually deserve one honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti is the plural of emeritus, a professor retired but keeping the title honorarily.

clue.text: Cheat German's wife and daughter

parts.note: Frau is German for wife or Mrs

explanation.surface: A man deceives his German spouse and their child.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is an impostor or swindler, someone who cheats.

clue.text: Stopped up with paperback, a mystery

parts.note: something stopped up is closed off
a paperback is a kind of book

explanation.surface: A blocked-up reader with a cheap novel, an enigma.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is an idiom for a subject or person one cannot understand, a mystery.

clue.text: Student left breadwinner

parts.note: a breadwinner is the family's earner

explanation.surface: A student who has left home to become the family's provider.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, a pupil or student.

clue.text: Unfortunate down-and-out in Rupert's place?

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the words down and out supply the letters, the joining and given nothing

explanation.surface: A destitute tramp in the home of someone called Rupert.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear, the long-running British children's comic-strip character, lives in the village of Nutwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutwood is the fictional English village that is home to Rupert Bear.

clue.text: Where youngsters play could make you spit!

definitions.text: Where youngsters play could make you spit!

parts.words: Where youngsters play could make you spit!
parts.note: a children's play area full of grit that ends up in little mouths, making them spit it out

explanation.surface: A playground spot that might leave you spitting in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a shallow box of sand where small children play, and sand in the mouth gets spat.

clue.text: Coloured cosmetics used before gathering for dancing game

parts.note: paint is an old word for coloured make-up
a ball is a formal social event with dancing

explanation.surface: Make-up applied before a dance, in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat game where players shoot pellets of dye at one another.

clue.text: Staff showing inordinate respect

indicators.note: inordinate literally means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Employees displaying excessive deference to the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is an ornamental rod or staff carried by a monarch.

clue.text: Enclosed den — not in cryptic style

parts.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed or enclosure on a letter
a lair is a wild animal's den

explanation.surface: A fenced-in animal den, described plainly rather than puzzlingly.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair, French for in clear, describes a message sent in plain language rather than code.

clue.text: Opening cut first

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a premiere is the opening night of a show or film

explanation.surface: The opening of a film was the first to be edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier as an adjective means first in rank or importance.

clue.text: Quickly passing over new English city

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece passes over, sitting above, the next

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for very quickly

explanation.surface: Rapidly moving above a newly built English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Oscar goes to silent film

indicators.note: goes to says the letter is added on to the end of the other piece

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak, silent
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Academy Award is given to a film from the silent era.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is the 1941 Disney animated film about a flying baby elephant.

clue.text: Extremely merry on organ? I strongly disagree

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outermost letters, of merry

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Being extremely jolly on the church organ, someone objects strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: My eye! is an old exclamation of disbelief, much like rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Kind, the French folk in court

indicators.note: the French article and folk are placed inside the letters for court

parts.note: le is French for the
men means people or folk

explanation.surface: Gentle French people appearing in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful and lenient, a kind disposition.

clue.text: Record number of competitors

definitions.meaning: an item written into a log or register
the field or total who signed up to take part in a contest

explanation.surface: A record turnout of contestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an item in a register, and the body of entrants in a contest.

clue.text: Guess capital of Somalia's very warm

indicators.note: capital here means the initial, upper-case letter of Somalia

parts.note: hot means very warm

explanation.surface: A guess about how hot Somalia's capital gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot, as in have a shot at it, is an attempt or guess.

clue.text: Account deficit above 500 — large amount

parts.note: over means above
D is the Roman numeral for 500
a raft of things is a large number or amount

explanation.surface: A bank account that is more than 500 short, a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is the deficit when more is withdrawn from a bank account than it holds.

clue.text: Instruct adult in college

indicators.note: the letter for adult is placed inside the college word

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Educate a grown-up at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct someone in a skill or subject.

clue.text: Guard part of castle

definitions.meaning: to look after, retain or protect something
the strongest central tower of a medieval fortress

explanation.surface: A sentry on duty in a section of the fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to guard or preserve, and the keep is a castle's main tower.

clue.text: Old lady collapsed in annexe, perhaps

parts.note: granny is an informal word for an old woman or grandmother
something collapsed is flattened, lying flat

explanation.surface: A grandmother has fallen over in the extension.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny flat is a British term for a self-contained annexe for an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny flat is often an annexe built onto a family home, so annexe is an example.
